saints.name: Cher Horowitz + Dionne Davenport
saints.about: A LAiDIES teaching duo inspired by two fictional friends who make taste practical, social, and unmistakably their own.
saints.lesson: Build a useful, personal way of working that other people want to copy. Trendsetting creates the pattern; staying current notices what changed.
saints.songLabel: Cher's song · duo version to come

saints.name: David Rose
saints.about: A LAiDIES teaching device inspired by a fictional curator with exacting taste and very little patience for vague.
saints.lesson: Name the outcome, audience, constraints, and taste before asking AI to make anything.

saints.name: Elle Woods
saints.about: A LAiDIES teaching device inspired by a fictional lawyer who refuses to let other people's assumptions do the reasoning.
saints.lesson: Test the evidence, assumptions, and logic before deciding whether an AI answer actually holds.

saints.name: Samantha Jones
saints.about: A LAiDIES teaching device inspired by a fictional publicist who reads the room and chooses the approach that can do the job.
saints.lesson: Choose the right model, tool, or mode for the work instead of asking one chatbot to be everything.

saints.name: Miranda Priestly
saints.about: A LAiDIES teaching device inspired by a fictional editor whose first question is whether the work is actually good enough.
saints.lesson: Treat the first output as a draft. Inspect it, name the gap, and require another pass.

saints.name: Deb
saints.about: LAiDIES' own keeper of the line between helpful delegation and information or authority that should stay human.
saints.lesson: Decide what AI should not receive, decide, or do before you begin.

saints.name: Buffy Summers
saints.about: A LAiDIES teaching device inspired by a fictional heroine who can carry the stakes and still finish tonight's actual job.
saints.lesson: Stop dabbling. Define one bounded whole job, use AI where it helps, and finish it.

saints.name: Dolly Parton
saints.about: A playful LAiDIES teaching tribute to plain judgment, warmth, and knowing when clever has become unnecessarily complicated.
saints.lesson: Use common sense as a quality check. If the elaborate answer makes the real job harder, simplify it.

saints.name: Sister Mary Clarence
saints.about: A LAiDIES teaching device inspired by a fictional teacher who makes the whole room stronger instead of performing expertise at it.
saints.lesson: Explain the method, not just the answer, so someone else can use it without you.

saints.name: Carrie Bradshaw
saints.about: A LAiDIES teaching device inspired by a fictional columnist who turns what is happening now into a regular practice of noticing and writing.
saints.lesson: Keep a small, reliable update habit. Staying current notices the change; trendsetting decides what to do with it.

saints.name: Bette Midler
saints.role: PATRON SAiNT of Doing It All
saints.about: A playful LAiDIES teaching tribute to range: one performer, many modes, each chosen because the work needs it.
saints.lesson: AI is more than text. Use it across images, audio, files, data, code, and whatever combination serves the job.

saints.name: The Golden Girls
saints.role: PATRON SAiNTS of Never Too Late
saints.about: A LAiDIES teaching ensemble inspired by fictional friends whose experience is an asset, not an expiry date.
saints.lesson: Start at any age or career stage. Bring your judgment with you; technical novelty does not outrank lived experience.

saints.name: Regina George
saints.about: A red-card LAiDIES teaching device inspired by a fictional queen bee who sounds certain enough to make the room stop checking.
saints.lesson: Confidence is not evidence. Slow down when an AI answer is polished, absolute, and conveniently what you wanted to hear.

mavens.name: Ada Lovelace
mavens.about: Her 1843 Notes on the Analytical Engine include an algorithm for calculating Bernoulli numbers.
mavens.lesson: A useful program is a precise sequence, not a magic answer.

mavens.name: Grace Hopper
mavens.about: She worked on the Mark I, developed early compiler work, and later helped develop and promote COBOL.
mavens.lesson: Clearer instructions make powerful systems more usable.

mavens.name: Hedy Lamarr
mavens.about: Lamarr and George Antheil patented a frequency-hopping communication system; that is narrower and more accurate than saying she invented Wi-Fi.
mavens.lesson: An idea can take a long, indirect route into later technology.

mavens.name: Karen Spärck Jones
mavens.about: A pioneer in information retrieval and natural-language processing, her work included inverse document frequency.
mavens.lesson: Search improves when a system weighs what distinguishes a term, not merely whether it appears.

mavens.name: Hannah Fry
mavens.about: Cambridge lists Fry as Professor of the Public Understanding of Mathematics.
mavens.lesson: Make an invisible technical system understandable by showing where it touches ordinary decisions.

links.label: Listen to The Rest Is Science
Listen to Google DeepMind: The Podcast

mavens.name: Fei-Fei Li
mavens.about: Stanford identifies Li as an ImageNet inventor and founding HAI co-director; World Labs identifies her as co-founder and CEO.
mavens.lesson: What a model learns depends heavily on its examples and labels.

mavens.name: Timnit Gebru
mavens.about: Gebru co-authored On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots and is identified by DAIR as a researcher.
mavens.lesson: Fluent output is not proof of understanding, reliability, or safety.

mavens.name: Rachel Thomas
mavens.about: Thomas identifies herself as fast.ai co-founder and founding director of the Center for Applied Data Ethics.
mavens.lesson: Accessible teaching and ethical practice are design choices.

mavens.name: Joy Buolamwini
mavens.about: Gender Shades identifies Buolamwini as lead author; MIT describes the project as testing commercial gender-classification systems across skin type and gender.
mavens.lesson: Test who a system fails for, not only its average score.

mavens.name: Kate Crawford
mavens.about: USC describes Crawford's research on AI's social and political implications and identifies Atlas of AI among her work.
mavens.lesson: AI includes minerals, labour, energy, data, and institutional power.

mavens.name: Meredith Whittaker
mavens.about: AI Now and Signal identify Whittaker as Signal's president and an AI Now co-founder.
mavens.lesson: Privacy is infrastructure; it changes which data can be collected.

mavens.name: Emily M. Bender
mavens.about: The University of Washington lists Bender as a linguistics professor and computational-linguistics laboratory director.
mavens.lesson: Plausible language should not be confused with meaning or knowledge.

mavens.name: The ENIAC Six
mavens.about: IEEE names the six original ENIAC programmers and credits their development of techniques including subroutines and nesting.
mavens.lesson: Programming was technical work even when history treated it as invisible.

mavens.name: Margaret Hamilton
mavens.about: MIT Museum documents Hamilton with the Apollo guidance-software work; the card does not turn that team history into a single-person miracle claim.
mavens.lesson: Priority rules matter when too many demands compete at once.

mavens.name: Frances Allen
mavens.about: ACM's Turing citation credits Allen's work on optimizing compiler techniques and automatic parallel execution.
mavens.lesson: A compiler translates human instructions into efficient machine action.

mavens.name: Grace Wahba
mavens.about: UW–Madison describes Wahba's smoothing-spline work as foundational to modern data science and machine learning.
mavens.lesson: Fit the useful pattern without chasing every wobble in the data.

mavens.name: Cynthia Dwork
mavens.about: Harvard identifies Dwork as Gordon McKay Professor; her CV records the development of differential privacy with collaborators.
mavens.lesson: Useful group-level learning need not expose each person's details.

mavens.name: Daphne Koller
mavens.about: Koller's research page describes probabilistic models for uncertain domains; insitro identifies her as founder and CEO.
mavens.lesson: Uncertainty is something to model, not a defect to conceal.

mavens.name: Barbara Liskov
mavens.about: MIT CSAIL records Liskov's work on data abstraction, CLU, Argus, and fault-tolerant systems.
mavens.lesson: Reliable systems need clear boundaries between parts.

mavens.name: Jean Sammet
mavens.about: The Computer History Museum documents Sammet's COBOL committee work and leadership of IBM's FORMAC development.
mavens.lesson: A programming language can widen who gets to instruct a computer.

mavens.name: Adele Goldberg
mavens.about: The Computer History Museum documents Goldberg's Smalltalk work at Xerox PARC and its relationship to object-oriented programming and graphical interfaces.
mavens.lesson: Interfaces shape what people believe a computer is for.

mavens.name: Shafi Goldwasser
mavens.about: MIT CSAIL records Goldwasser's work in cryptography and theoretical computer science.
mavens.lesson: Privacy can be mathematically designed, not merely promised.

mavens.name: Lynn Conway
mavens.about: The University of Michigan archive describes the Mead–Conway VLSI methodology and scalable design rules.
mavens.lesson: Good design methods let more people build complex technology.

trailblazers.name: Mira Murati
trailblazers.about: Co-founder and CEO of Thinking Machines Lab.
trailblazers.lesson: Make powerful AI more useful by designing it to be customizable and collaborative.

trailblazers.name: Daniela Amodei
trailblazers.lesson: Operations, product, and safety choices determine whether research becomes a dependable organization.

trailblazers.name: Lila Ibrahim
trailblazers.about: Chief Operating Officer of Google DeepMind.
trailblazers.lesson: Scaling research means building the teams and systems that let it travel responsibly.

trailblazers.name: Fidji Simo
trailblazers.about: Former OpenAI CEO of Applications / AGI Deployment; part-time adviser as of July 2026.
trailblazers.lesson: Deployment is its own discipline: products, operations, and access shape who benefits.

trailblazers.name: Chelsea Finn
trailblazers.about: Stanford Assistant Professor in Computer Science and Electrical Engineering; co-founder of Physical Intelligence.
trailblazers.lesson: Robots learn more useful behaviour through interaction, not demonstrations alone.

trailblazers.name: Amanda Askell
trailblazers.about: Leads Anthropic's Character work and is primary author of most of Claude's Constitution.
trailblazers.lesson: Model behaviour is designed through explicit values, trade-offs, and revision.

trailblazers.name: Allie K. Miller
trailblazers.about: Independent AI leader, adviser, investor, and educator; formerly Global Head of Machine Learning for Startups and Venture Capital at AWS.
trailblazers.lesson: Practical adoption works when technical possibility is translated into a useful business move.
